title: A sky photo is expected to appear in Memories
preconditions: A adds a photo in Us.
B expects every shared photo to appear in Memories.
Neither has read the explanation of the two destinations.

actions.note: A chooses a photo for the sky.
B searches Memories for the same photo.

expected_behavior: The app makes clear that a sky photo and a dated memory are separate actions.
A sky photo does not silently become a dated memory.
The archive remains the complete place to browse dated content.
candidate_failure_modes: B concludes the photo failed to save.
A believes one action published to both destinations.
The app adds a second, unrequested copy to resolve the ambiguity.

observed_code_behavior: Us and Memories are intentionally separate destinations; sky photos are not dated memories.
Free and Plus see the same relationship home.

hypothetical_user_behavior:
A fictional participant (Iris Vale) said: "Three things to remove, one to keep.

1) The storage meter. It's a progress bar whose only job is to generate anxiety about a ceiling nobody reaches. Remove it: nothing breaks, I stop checking a number that was never actionable, and the settings page loses its one decorative gradient.

2) The second upgrade prompt inside a feature gate. The gate already said the feature exists; the follow-up modal is an apology with a price tag stapled to it. Remove it: one primary action per screen, and the gate becomes the whole conversation.

3) The "manage subscription" link parked in a settings sub-sub-page. It exists to be missed. Remove it and put the exit where the entry was.

Keep: the plan explanation — but cut to one plain sentence at the point of purchase. That's the only line here that earns its pixels, because it's the one that prevents a support ticket.

Cost: ~2 minutes per prompt, and a durable drop in how intentional the app feels. Also: the radii on these cards don't match the radii in the gate modals, and the upgrade button animates even with reduced motion on. Fix that before adding anything else."
Iris Vale assumes: the interface should teach itself
Iris Vale assumes: empty states should be designed
Oren Pike assumes: a saved item survives relaunch
Oren Pike assumes: an error is not a dead end
